name: WCXB: A Multi-Type Web Content Extraction Benchmark (Murrough Foley et al., arXiv:2605.21097, May 2026)
kind: Benchmark (dataset + evaluation harness + leaderboard). Not a library or standard; the object under study for this project is what its reporting methodology implies extraction evaluations should look like.
maturity: Research artifact, first release May 2026, actively maintained (leaderboard site webcontentextraction.org, GitHub repo, HuggingFace dataset mirror). Too new to have a second edition or independent replications yet.
license: Dataset released CC-BY-4.0 (HTML source files, JSON ground truth, page-type labels, dev/test split, baseline results). Permits use in this project including derivative evaluation, with attribution.
keeps_and_discards: Not an extractor itself -- it is the yardstick. Ground truth marks the 'main content' span per page as word-bag text; everything the pipeline classifies as boilerplate (nav, ads, related-links rails, comment widgets unless the page type is 'forum' in which case comment threads ARE the content) is excluded from the reference. The word-bag comparison discards whitespace, paragraph order and formatting by design (justified in the paper as noise orthogonal to extraction quality), so it cannot score structural fidelity -- only lexical coverage.
structure_preserved: None preserved in the metric itself -- word-level bag-of-tokens F1 explicitly ignores order, nesting, and formatting. The dataset does retain page-type labels (7 types: article, forum, product, collection, listing, documentation, service) which is a structural signal about the SOURCE page, but the scoring function does not check whether an extractor preserved tabular relations, list structure or shadow boundaries.
interactive_elements: Out of scope. WCXB pages are static HTML snapshots; no interactive controls are part of ground truth or scoring.
interactive_state_fidelity: Not applicable -- the benchmark has no notion of control state (disabled/checked/expanded/aria). It is a pure text-content boundary benchmark, not an interface-fidelity benchmark.
layout_awareness: The dataset does not encode geometry; ground truth is defined over the DOM/HTML text, not rendered layout. Systems under test (Trafilatura, Readability, etc.) may internally use layout heuristics, but WCXB's own harness runs on static HTML source, not a rendered page, so layout-dependent behavior of an extractor is not separately measured.
javascript_required: No -- the corpus is static HTML source files ('static HTML only' per the paper's own Limitations Section 8, item 2: no live JavaScript-heavy SPAs except flagged empty entries). This means WCXB cannot evaluate extractors, like a real browser-based serializer, on pages whose main content is client-rendered.
evaluation_method: Word-level F1 against a human-adjudicated ground-truth span, computed as bag-of-words overlap (lowercased, split on non-alphanumeric characters) between extracted text and reference text -- explicitly not a sequence metric like ROUGE-L, chosen because whitespace/order differences across extractors are treated as extraction-irrelevant noise. This is a REFERENCE-based (oracle) evaluation, the opposite pole from the project's own oracle-free interest.
corpus_size_and_origins: 2,008 pages total from 1,613 unique domains, collected September 2025 to March 2026 via Common Crawl archives, ChatNoir web search, and manual curation. Split into 1,497-page dev set and 511-page held-out test set with matched page-type distribution across the 7 types (article 53% of pages, N=793; service N=165; forum N=113; collection N=117; listing N=99; product N=119; documentation N=91, 6.1% of the corpus -- the smallest category). Median domain contributes 1 page; 95th percentile contributes 3 pages, i.e. deliberately domain-diverse rather than domain-repeated. This dwarfs CleanEval's 58 pages from 2007 in both count and origin count, and post-dates it by ~19 years, but remains English-dominant and static-HTML-only.
reported_precision_recall: Overall (all page types) F1 = 0.859 for the best system on the full corpus vs. 0.932 for the same system restricted to articles only -- a 7.3-point gap the paper uses as its headline finding. Per-type F1 for the six baselines reported in Table 7 (denominator = page count per type): rs-trafilatura leads on 5 of 7 types -- article 0.932 (n=793), documentation 0.931 (n=91), service 0.843 (n=165), forum 0.792 (n=113), collection 0.713 (n=117), listing 0.704 (n=99), product 0.670 (n=119). No system exceeds F1=0.80 on forums, 0.72 on collections, or 0.68 on products across ALL 13 systems tested (11 heuristic: rs-trafilatura, Resiliparse, Trafilatura, dom-smoothie, Newspaper4k, magic-html, jusText, BoilerPy3, Readability, Goose3, dom-content-extraction; 2 neural: MinerU-HTML/Qwen3-0.6B, ReaderLM-v2/1.5B).
independent_oracle: No independent oracle beyond the ground-truth-vs-extraction comparison itself; ground truth is LLM-assisted (Claude drafts, four independent Claude Opus review passes, automated schema/bounds/snippet checks) with a SINGLE human reviewer performing final adjudication. The paper is explicit that this is a limitation, not a strength (see reported_precision_recall / evaluation_method context and constraint discussion below).
evidence_independence: Independent of any single extractor vendor -- authored by third-party researchers (Murrough Foley et al.) evaluating 13 competing tools, none of which they appear to be commercial stakeholders in. This is the most vendor-neutral evaluation among the items in this research set, in contrast to most HTML-to-markdown comparisons which are run by the tool's own authors.
page_archetype_coverage: This IS the benchmark's central contribution: 7 page-type archetypes (article, forum, product, collection, listing, documentation, service) with per-type F1 reported for every system, explicitly designed to expose the 0.93-to-0.41-0.84 spread that single-aggregate article-only benchmarks (CleanEval etc.) cannot detect. The paper's headline number (0.859 overall vs 0.932 article-only) is precisely the number this project's fields.yaml `page_archetype_coverage` field description references.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Predominantly English; the paper states extraction systems 'may perform differently on non-English content' and flags 'multilingual expansion... planned for future versions' as an open gap. No CJK/RTL/whitespace-free-segmentation breakdown exists in this release -- word-bag tokenization ('split on non-alphanumeric characters') is itself a Latin-script-biased design choice that would misbehave on scripts without whitespace-delimited words (e.g. Chinese, Japanese, Thai).
leaks_outward: Not applicable in the sense of runtime telemetry -- WCXB is an offline dataset/benchmark harness, not a live capture tool. No network egress from the pages being scored (they are static HTML files).
mechanism_detectability: Not applicable -- the corpus is static HTML processed offline; there is no live page from whose perspective detectability could be assessed.
countermeasures: Not applicable -- no adversarial or fingerprinting concern in a static-file benchmark.
measured_fidelity_cost: Not applicable in the privacy-hardening sense. The closest analogue is the accuracy cost of ignoring JavaScript-rendered content: because the corpus is static-HTML-only, the benchmark cannot measure the fidelity cost of NOT executing scripts, which is a real gap for any browser-based serializer being evaluated against it.
gate_state_at_capture: Not tracked at all -- the paper's Limitations section does not mention paywalls, consent banners or login walls as a sampling concern, and since pages were pulled from Common Crawl/ChatNoir/manual curation as static snapshots, gated content likely could not be captured properly in the first place (a Common-Crawl-sourced corpus systematically under-samples paywalled/gated pages, though this bias is not quantified in the paper).
determinism: Not directly stated for the scoring harness itself (word-bag F1 computation is deterministic given fixed inputs), but the GROUND TRUTH construction is not fully deterministic/reproducible in the sense of independent replication, since it depends on LLM (Claude) outputs at drafting and multi-pass review stages -- the paper does not claim a second independently-constructed ground truth would match.
determinism_across_versions: Not addressed. The paper does not test whether re-running the same 13 extraction tools at a later library version reproduces the reported scores; given several of the tools (Trafilatura, Readability forks) are actively developed, score drift across tool versions is a plausible unexamined risk.
reproducibility: High for the artifact itself: HTML source files, JSON ground truth, page-type labels, dev/test splits and baseline extraction outputs are all released under CC-BY-4.0, so the reported numbers can be recomputed exactly. Reproducibility of the GROUND TRUTH construction process is explicitly NOT claimed -- inter-annotator agreement is not reported, and the paper states plainly: 'We cannot report formal inter-annotator agreement metrics... subjectivity in content boundary decisions remains unquantified.'
failure_modes: Documented per-type collapse on structured pages: F1 falls to 0.41-0.84 range for forum/product/collection/listing types versus 0.93 for articles, meaning every tested heuristic and neural extractor systematically under- or over-extracts on non-article page shapes. The paper attributes this to page types whose 'main content' boundary is inherently more ambiguous (e.g. product pages mixing description, reviews, and spec tables) and to training/tuning bias toward article-shaped pages in the extractors themselves.
failure_visibility: Loud, by design -- the entire point of the benchmark is to make per-type failure visible rather than averaged away; the paper explicitly frames the aggregate-vs-article-only gap as evidence that single-aggregate reporting HIDES failure. This is the closest thing in this research set to a project-aligned methodological result.
scale_limits: Not a running system with a scale axis -- it is a fixed 2,008-page corpus. No claim about how evaluation cost scales; word-bag F1 computation is linear in token count per page, trivially cheap.
delta_cost_model: Not applicable -- WCXB is a static, one-shot evaluation corpus with no notion of incremental page change or delta cost.
reanchoring_stability: Not applicable -- no re-anchoring concept; ground truth is a fixed text span per fixed HTML snapshot, never re-anchored against a mutated DOM.
adversarial_exposure: Not evaluated -- WCXB has no injection/adversarial-content page type or scoring dimension; its page types are structural/genre categories (article, forum, product, etc.), not threat categories. A prompt-injection payload embedded as normal-looking body text would simply be scored as content to extract or not, with no special handling.
provenance_carrying: The dataset itself carries page-level provenance (URL, page-type label, collection source) but the F1 SCORING METRIC discards all per-token provenance -- word-bag comparison has no concept of xpath, capture time or origin per token. Not a provenance-preserving evaluation.
roundtrip_safety: Not evaluated -- no serialize-then-reparse round-trip check exists in the WCXB methodology; it is a one-directional extraction-accuracy benchmark.
token_budget_and_ordering: Not evaluated -- the word-bag metric explicitly discards ORDER as noise, which is the opposite assumption from what an SLM-facing ordering contract needs. WCXB cannot be used to assess whether an extractor places high-value content early in a truncated context window.
representation_cost: Not reported -- no token-count-per-page or compression-ratio figures are part of the WCXB methodology; it measures content-boundary accuracy only, not representation efficiency.
what_could_be_adopted: Adopt the METHODOLOGY, not the tool: (1) per-archetype reporting instead of a single aggregate score -- this project should classify its own evaluation pages by the same or an analogous 7-type taxonomy (or its own equivalent) and report a per-type table rather than one number, exactly because WCXB shows a 0.93-to-0.41 spread an aggregate hides; (2) explicit acknowledgment of unquantified annotator subjectivity as a stated limitation rather than an implied precision; (3) the CC-BY-4.0 released HTML+ground-truth corpus itself could be reused as one input distribution for testing this project's own dedup/extraction fold against known-content-boundary pages, though it cannot validate interactive-state or layout-blind-fold behavior since it is static-HTML-only and text-boundary-only.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY -- WCXB's ground truth is itself produced by LLM-driven boundary judgment (a structure/region classifier by another name), so it cannot certify a structure-agnostic approach as correct, only reveal where a structure-agnostic approach's OUTPUT happens to diverge from a heuristic notion of 'main content.' no_layout_in_the_fold: NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY -- ground truth is defined over static HTML text, not geometry, so it cannot test whether a layout-blind fold correctly excludes visually-hidden content; it would score hidden-but-textually-present injected content as either correctly or incorrectly extracted with no visibility into WHY. o_delta: NOT APPLICABLE -- no incremental-update concept in the benchmark. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS AS A REAL-CORPUS SOURCE -- the released HTML files are real captured pages, not synthetic/mocked fixtures, so using them as replay input violates nothing. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NOT APPLICABLE -- static HTML source files predate any live shadow-DOM capture question. OVERALL VERDICT: adoptable in the actuator/evaluation layer only, specifically as (a) a source of real diverse-archetype HTML fixtures and (b) a template for per-archetype score reporting; never as a certifier of structure-agnostic or layout-blind correctness, since its own ground truth embeds exactly the kind of region-naming judgment this project's structure_agnosticism constraint refuses to compute.
governance_signal_handling: Not addressed in the paper. Collection via Common Crawl inherits Common Crawl's own robots.txt-respecting crawl policy, but WCXB's own paper does not discuss robots.txt, ai.txt, or licensing-signal handling for the pages it redistributes as CC-BY-4.0 HTML source, which is a notable gap given the pages themselves were presumably copyrighted by their original sites.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Not addressed -- the paper does not discuss PII handling or lawful basis for retaining full HTML source of 2,008 real third-party web pages under a CC-BY-4.0 re-release, which is a live open question the WCXB authors do not engage with (distinct from the CC-BY-4.0 license they apply to their OWN annotations/labels vs. the underlying page content's original copyright status).
uncertain: reported_precision_recall (precision/recall broken out per system beyond F1 was not fully extracted from the paper; only F1 per type for 6 of 13 systems was confirmed from the fetched table)
determinism (ground-truth LLM-drafting determinism was not directly tested by the paper; inferred from its own stated inter-annotator-agreement gap)
legal_basis_and_pii_posture (paper does not discuss this; absence itself is the finding, not a confirmed position)
governance_signal_handling (inferred from Common Crawl's general policy, not confirmed against the WCXB paper directly)
